articles.title_original: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
articles.title_zh: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
facts_zh:
Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war
- Published
Ethiopia's government and the party in control of the northern region of Tigray have accused each other of launching offensives, escalating fears of a return to full-scale conflict.

Getachew Reda, a cabinet minister and adviser to Ethiopia's prime minister, said Tigrayan fighters had taken control of federally administered airports in Tigray and launched offensives in neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions.
Earlier, the Tigrayan authorities said their forces had been forced to enter a "defensive war".

all_titles.en: Ethiopia and Tigray accuse each of launching offensives, fuelling fears of new war

facts_zh:
Azerbaijan pardons Frenchman after EU lifts sanctions on Russian billionaire
- Published
French national Martin Ryan has been pardoned and his release from prison ordered by Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev after he was jailed on charges of spying.
His release came hours after the EU agreed to lift sanctions on two Russian billionaires, prompting anger from Ukraine.
Diplomats had indicated that France had pushed for an end to restrictions on one of the businessmen, Alisher Usmanov.

articles.title_zh: Eleven killed in mass shooting at house in South Africa
facts_zh:
Eleven killed in mass shooting at house in South Africa
- Published
At least 11 people have been killed in a mass shooting in a residential building near the South African city of Durban.
Gunmen stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township late on Tuesday and opened fire on 14 people.
Ten were killed at the scene and four were taken to hospital, where one later died from their injuries, police said.

articles.title_zh: Angry Anderson, rock star who soundtracked Kylie's wedding in Neighbours, dies aged 79
facts_zh:
Angry Anderson, rock star who soundtracked Kylie's wedding in Neighbours, dies aged 79
- Published
Rock star Angry Anderson, whose music famously soundtracked the wedding of Kylie Minogue and Jason Donovan's characters in Australian TV soap Neighbours, has died at the age of 79.
The musician, whose real name was Gary Anderson, rose to fame as the frontman of Rose Tattoo, one of Australia's most revered rock bands, from 1976.
His solo song Suddenly became a global hit after it was played during the wedding of Minogue and Donovan's characters Scott and Charlene in Neighbours.

articles.title_zh: Hurricane Polo downgraded but remains 'very powerful' off coast of Mexico
facts_zh:
Hurricane Polo downgraded but remains 'very powerful' off coast of Mexico
- Published
Hurricane Polo, a large storm off the coast of Mexico, has been downgraded to category 4 but remains "very powerful", the US National Hurricane Center said.
The Pacific hurricane, one of the strongest of the season, was projected to head towards the coast of south-western Mexico, bringing intense wind and rain, though was not expected to make landfall.

A Hurricane Hunter aircraft, operated by the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa), flew into the storm on Tuesday and recorded sustained wind speeds near 180 mph (285 km/h), with stronger gusts.

all_titles.en: Hurricane Polo downgraded but remains 'very powerful' off coast of Mexico

articles.title_zh: Dolly Parton's manager accuses her nephew of 'threats and intimidation'
facts_zh:
Dolly Parton's manager accuses her nephew of 'threats and intimidation'
- Published
Dolly Parton's management company has accused her nephew of "threats, intimidation, and coercion", revealing a bitter battle over the late star's legacy and business interests.
The accusations against Bryan Seaver, who was Parton's head of security and was handpicked to announce her death last month, have been made public in US legal documents filed this week.
The company that manages Parton's businesses and properties, She's Alive, is seeking a temporary civil restraining order against him.

all_titles.en: Dolly Parton's manager accuses her nephew of 'threats and intimidation'

articles.title_original: OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine
articles.title_zh: OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine
facts_zh:
OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine
- Published
The tech giant OpenAI will share its AI cyber defence system Daybreak for free with the Ukraine government to help it protect civilian infrastructure, like hospitals and power plants, from cyber-attacks.
According to the Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA), the national cyber incident response team, Ukraine recorded nearly 6,000 attacks in 2025.
Daybreak is able to quickly identify weaknesses in digital systems and help develop fixes.

all_titles.en: OpenAI gives cyber defence tools to Ukraine

articles.title_original: South Sudan's president dissolves government ahead of country's first elections
articles.title_zh: South Sudan's president dissolves government ahead of country's first elections
facts_zh:
South Sudan's president dissolves government ahead of country's first elections
- Published
South Sudan President Salva Kiir has dissolved the transitional government, three months before the country's first election since its independence in 2011.
The country has previously postponed elections twice and extended the transitional period several times.
Under the amended law, signed on Monday, Kiir removed the country's five vice-presidents and dissolved parliament, as well as national and state governments.

all_titles.en: South Sudan's president dissolves government ahead of country's first elections

Trump meets US-backed Venezuelan president for first time since Maduro seized
- Published
US President Donald Trump has held talks with Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodríguez at the UN General Assembly, their first face-to-face meeting since the White House backed her to take over the South American country's government.
Rodríguez succeeded Nicolás Maduro shortly after US forces conducted a raid on the Venezuelan capital Caracas and seized him.
The pair met a few kilometres from the New York jail where Maduro is awaiting trial for drug trafficking and other charges.

articles.title_original: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds
articles.title_zh: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds
facts_zh:
Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds
- Published
There has been a sharp rise in reports of violence against women and girls in the Gaza Strip, including early and forced marriage, according to a series of recent reports from the UN Population Fund (UNFPA).

One report, which analyses data collected by 10 organisations, says, external the protracted crisis in war-torn Gaza has "created conditions in which women and girls face escalating risks of gender-based violence".
It also warns that there has been a "severe escalation" in the number of early and forced marriage incidents in the second quarter of this year.

all_titles.en: Reports of violence against women in Gaza surge, UN agency finds

articles.title_original: More than 170,000 respiratory cases recorded in haze-choked Indonesia
articles.title_zh: More than 170,000 respiratory cases recorded in haze-choked Indonesia
facts_zh:
More than 170,000 respiratory cases recorded in haze-choked Indonesia
- Published
Some 175,000 people in Indonesia have suffered from respiratory illness since August, its health ministry said, as it continues to battle wildfires that have raged for weeks.
More than 40,000 cases – which range from coughs to bronchitis and more serious conditions like pneumonia – involve toddlers.
Forest fires have blanketed parts of the country as well as neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore in toxic smog, pushing air quality indices into "unhealthy" territory.

all_titles.en: More than 170,000 respiratory cases recorded in haze-choked Indonesia

The defence lawyer for a Massachusetts mother accused of murdering her three children has asked a judge to investigate a juror in the case.
The proceedings against Lindsay Clancy ended in a mistrial and acrimony this month after the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict.
Her attorney, Kevin Reddington, wants the court to probe mobile phone use by "Juror Doe" during deliberations as well as a questionnaire he filled out.
